ANF.headline: Abercrombie: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
ANF.description: Abercrombie & Fitch reported Q3 2026 earnings with 11% net sales growth to $1.4 billion, marking its 16th consecutive quarter of growth. The company achieved higher average unit retail (AUR) through tight inventory control and reduced promotions. New smaller store formats are delivering twice the productivity of closed locations, while wholesale partnerships expand market reach. Management raised full-year guidance and plans at least $500 million in share repurchases.

ANF.headline: Abercrombie & Fitch (ANF) Tops Q3 Earnings and Revenue Estimates
ANF.description: Abercrombie & Fitch reported Q3 earnings of $3.82 per share, beating consensus estimates by 21.27%, with revenues of $1.44 billion exceeding expectations by 4.94%. The stock has gained 11.6% year-to-date, outperforming the S&P 500's 5.7% gain. However, the company received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating due to mixed estimate revisions, suggesting near-term performance in line with the market. The retail apparel industry remains in the bottom 40% of Zacks-ranked industries.

ANF.headline: 5 Retail and Tech Earnings Charts to Watch This Week
ANF.description: As third quarter 2026 earnings season winds down, five companies with strong earnings track records are reporting this week during the critical holiday shopping season. Best Buy, Abercrombie & Fitch, Dycom Industries, Dell Technologies, and Urban Outfitters have all demonstrated consistent earnings beats over the past five years, though some face recent stock price headwinds from market sell-offs.

KYMR.headline: Kymera Shares Soar 30% After Positive Atopic Dermatitis Drug Data
KYMR.description: Kymera Therapeutics announced positive results from its BROADEN2 phase IIb trial of KT-621, an investigational oral STAT6 degrader for moderate to severe atopic dermatitis. The mid-dose group achieved a 72% EASI reduction versus 27% for placebo, with significant itch relief and rapid onset of activity. The company plans to advance into phase III development by mid-2027, with potential to compete against established biologics like Dupixent.

KYMR.headline: Kymera Therapeutics Announces Pricing of Upsized $1.75 Billion Public Offering
KYMR.description: Kymera Therapeutics priced an underwritten public offering of $1.75 billion, selling 11.64 million shares at $150.37 per share. The clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company plans to use net proceeds to advance its pipeline of oral small molecule degrader programs for immunological diseases. The offering is expected to close on November 25, 2026.

KYMR.headline: Kymera Therapeutics Announces Proposed Public Offering
KYMR.description: Kymera Therapeutics, a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, announced an underwritten public offering of $1.5 billion in common stock, with an additional $225 million option for underwriters. The company plans to use proceeds to advance its pipeline of targeted protein degradation (TPD) degrader programs for immunological diseases and general corporate purposes.

NVDA.headline: ROSEN, RECOGNIZED INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages NVIDIA Corporation Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action First Filed by the Firm - NVDA
NVDA.description: Rosen Law Firm has filed a securities class action lawsuit against NVIDIA Corporation, alleging that company executives made false and misleading statements regarding relationships with individuals connected to national security concerns and potential policy violations. The lawsuit covers investors who purchased NVIDIA securities between December 19, 2024 and November 12, 2026, with a lead plaintiff deadline of January 8, 2027.

NVDA.headline: Dell Just Reported Earnings and Raised Its Forecast by $10 Billion. Is the Stock a Buy After Tuesday's Selloff?
NVDA.description: Dell Technologies reported Q3 revenue of $54.9 billion (up 103% YoY) and raised its full-year forecast by $10 billion to $202 billion, driven by strong AI server sales which tripled to $22 billion. Despite a 12% stock decline on Tuesday following HPE's margin warnings, Dell's gross margins actually improved to 21% and infrastructure operating margins rose to 17%. The stock trades at 10x forward earnings with a record $132.3 billion AI backlog covering two-thirds of expected annual revenue.

NVDA.headline: Stock Market Today, Nov. 24: Tech Sell-Off Drags Nasdaq as Dow Gains on Value Rotation
NVDA.description: The stock market showed mixed performance on November 24, 2026, as investors rotated from technology into value and defensive sectors. The Nasdaq fell 1.48% due to cooling AI momentum, while the Dow Jones gained 0.85% on strength in healthcare and consumer stocks. Major tech names like Nvidia declined 5.86%, while retailers Kohl's and Dollar Tree surged on strong earnings beats.

NVDA.headline: Why Anthropic Stock Fell Again
NVDA.description: Anthropic stock dropped 6.6% on November 24, 2026, falling below its $83 IPO price for the first time since its debut last week. The decline reflects broader concerns about the long-term profitability of frontier AI companies. Despite a brief market rally following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's reinstatement announcement, investor optimism has waned as questions mount about the economics of AI companies like Anthropic.

NVDA.headline: Stock Market Today, Nov. 24: Nvidia Gives Back $240 Billion in Market Value Despite Wall Street Upgrade Signaling 29% Upside
NVDA.description: Nvidia fell 5.86% on November 24, erasing a portion of Monday's historic 31.48% surge following CEO Jensen Huang's reinstatement. Despite the pullback, the semiconductor industry faced renewed selling pressure. Wall Street remains optimistic with Bernstein upgrading Nvidia to Outperform with a $200 price target, implying 29% upside. The company's strong Q3 revenue of $115.8 billion (103% YoY growth) and raised guidance suggest underlying fundamentals remain solid despite short-term volatility.

NVDA.headline: Did Nvidia Make a Big Mistake by Reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO so Quickly?
NVDA.description: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO less than two weeks after his resignation, a sharp reversal from earlier statements. The decision was reportedly influenced by the U.S. president and market pressure as Nvidia's stock plummeted. However, the quick reinstatement raises governance concerns, as an investigation into Huang's involvement with a possible Chinese spy remains ongoing, and he is still scheduled to meet with Congress.

NVDA.headline: Axon Enterprise vs. Palantir Technologies: Which Law Enforcement Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
NVDA.description: Comparing two high-growth law enforcement and data analytics companies, Axon Enterprise and Palantir Technologies. While Palantir shows stronger revenue growth (87.1% vs 33.6%), Axon trades at a lower valuation premium and offers more sustainable growth with improving margins. The analyst recommends Axon for 2027 despite Palantir's impressive top-line expansion, citing concerns about Palantir's exceptional valuation and potential AI displacement risks.

NVDA.headline: Anthropic Stock Just Broke Below Its $83 IPO Price. Is It a Bargain Buy?
NVDA.description: Anthropic's stock fell below its $83 IPO price on its fourth trading day of trading, despite opening at $111.50. While the company shows exceptional revenue growth ($1.4B to $17B YoY in Q3), the analyst expresses concerns about its 41x sales valuation, rising compute costs (58% of Q3 sales), and lack of competitive moat. The company turned a $974M Q2 operating profit into a $567M Q3 loss, raising questions about long-term profitability despite impressive growth metrics.

NVDA.headline: Should Vanguard S&P 500 ETF Investors Be Worried About the Downturn in Nvidia and AI Stocks?
NVDA.description: Nvidia and AI stocks have significantly dragged down the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF this month, with Nvidia down 32% from its October high following CEO Jensen Huang's surprise resignation and subsequent return. However, the article advises against selling S&P 500 ETF holdings, noting that the index's self-correcting structure allows other leaders to emerge and that long-term dollar-cost averaging remains a proven strategy despite short-term volatility.

NVDA.headline: 4 PEG-Based Value Stocks to Buy as NVIDIA Leads Wall Street Rebound
NVDA.description: Following NVIDIA's strong rebound and tech sector rally, investors are advised to look beyond momentum stocks and identify fundamentally sound companies trading at attractive valuations. The article discusses a PEG-ratio-based screening strategy to avoid value traps and highlights four stocks that meet the criteria: Arrow Electronics, Super Micro Computer, BP, and Ingram Micro.

UMC.headline: TSM's AI-Driven Growth Accelerates: Is There More Upside Ahead?
UMC.description: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM) reported Q3 2026 revenues of $46.72 billion, up 41.2% year-over-year, driven by strong AI infrastructure demand. HPC contributed 68% of revenues, while 2-nanometer technology reached 8% of wafer sales. TSM expects full-year 2026 revenue growth of 44% and plans to more than double N2 capacity in 2027. Competitors UMC and Intel also reported strong performance, with UMC's revenues up 25.6% and Intel's Data Center and AI revenues surging 78%.

ASX.headline: Are Computer and Technology Stocks Lagging  ASE Technology (ASX) This Year?
ASX.description: ASE Technology Hldg (ASX) has significantly outperformed the Computer and Technology sector year-to-date, gaining 63.2% compared to the sector's -6.2% decline. The stock holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with improving analyst sentiment, as consensus earnings estimates have risen 8.3% over the past 90 days. Amphenol (APH) is another sector outperformer with a 3.2% year-to-date return and similar positive earnings revision trends.

ASX.headline: LSCC Rides on Balanced Organic & Inorganic Growth: Should You Buy?
ASX.description: Lattice Semiconductor (LSCC) reported Q3 revenues of $291 million, up 118.3% year-over-year, driven by strong AI infrastructure demand and FPGA growth. The company's industrial segment revenues rose 34.9%, with expected acceleration to 70% in Q4. The AMI acquisition contributed $39.1 million in Q3 revenues, expanding Lattice's AI server and security capabilities. The stock has gained 43.6% over the past year and holds a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) rating.

MRVL.headline: MaxLinear Stock Drops 24% in a Month: Should You Buy it on the Dip?
MRVL.description: MaxLinear (MXL) shares dropped 24.3% in a month due to semiconductor supply constraints, rising debt, and negative operating cash flow. However, strong AI infrastructure demand, robust order visibility extending into 2028, and upward earnings estimate revisions (15% increase in 30 days) support long-term growth prospects. The stock trades at a premium to the sector but offers an attractive entry point for long-term investors.

MRVL.headline: Credo's Optical Expansion: Can It Gain Ground Against Rivals?
MRVL.description: Credo Technology (CRDO) is capitalizing on AI-driven demand for optical connectivity solutions, expecting optical revenues to exceed $600 million in fiscal 2027. The company's optical DSP business posted record Q1 revenues, with ZeroFlap Optics, silicon photonics PICs, and optical DSPs each projected to contribute over $100 million. However, CRDO shares have declined 45.6% in three months and trade at a premium valuation compared to peers, earning a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

MRVL.headline: Marvell Stock Fell Almost 12% in a Single Day. I'd Consider Buying Shares Now.
MRVL.description: Marvell Technology's stock dropped nearly 12% to $122.28 on November 20, primarily due to concerns about its announced acquisition of Lumentum Holdings. However, the analyst argues the sell-off is overdone given the company's accelerating data center business, which is growing at 75% year-over-year and now represents 79% of revenue. Trading at around 20x fiscal 2028 earnings, Marvell is valued near market average despite significantly above-average growth prospects, making it an attractive buyin

MRVL.headline: Why Marvell Technology Stock Crushed it Today
MRVL.description: Marvell Technology stock surged 18.37% on November 23, 2026, following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's reinstatement. The rally was driven by investor confidence that the existing business relationship between the two companies would continue. Nvidia had previously invested $2 billion in Marvell, highlighting their collaborative importance in the AI chip market.

MRVL.headline: Should You Buy Marvell Technology Stock Before Dec. 1?
MRVL.description: Marvell Technology reports earnings on December 1 with forecasted 50%+ revenue growth already priced into the stock. The article suggests waiting until after earnings to buy, citing concerns about rising interest rates potentially reducing tech spending, the controversial $115 billion Lumentum acquisition, and the stock's current 50x trailing earnings valuation being difficult to justify given economic headwinds.

MRVL.headline: 3 Millionaire-Maker AI Chip Stocks Wall Street Isn't Talking About
MRVL.description: The article highlights three smaller AI chip stocks with potential for market-beating returns: Marvell Technology, which specializes in ASIC and interconnect chips for data centers; Silicon Motion Technology, a NAND flash controller supplier experiencing explosive growth; and Qualcomm, an established chipmaker entering the AI data center market with major partnerships and a low valuation.

MRVL.headline: Arm vs. Marvell Technology: Which Artificial Intelligence Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
MRVL.description: The article compares Arm Holdings and Marvell Technology as AI investment opportunities through 2027. Arm dominates mobile through IP licensing with high margins but faces valuation concerns and risks from open-source alternatives. Marvell specializes in data center networking infrastructure with lower valuations and stronger growth prospects, though it carries customer concentration and integration risks from its Lumentum acquisition. SKHY.headline: Billionaire Philippe Laffont of Coatue Management Sent AMD Shares Packing and Loaded Up on This Hot AI IPO Instead
SKHY.description: Billionaire investor Philippe Laffont of Coatue Management completely exited his position in Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) in Q3 2026 after holding 14 million shares, citing profit-taking and concerns about AMD's high valuation and limited AI GPU market share. Instead, Laffont invested approximately $1.75 billion in SK Hynix (SKHY), an AI IPO that supplies high-bandwidth memory (HBM) critical for AI infrastructure, benefiting from strong demand and supply shortages expected to persist through 203

SKHY.headline: Why SK Hynix Stock Skyrocketed Today
SKHY.description: SK Hynix stock surged 20% after reports that SoftBank Group's Chairman Masayoshi Son explored acquiring the chipmaker for $1 trillion. The proposed deal, which would have given SoftBank control over key AI semiconductor supply chain components, ultimately did not proceed due to regulatory concerns and the deal's massive scale. SK Hynix stock remains attractively priced at less than 7 times earnings, though concerns persist about maintaining profit margins amid AI market volatility.

CBRS.headline: Anthropic Just Went Public. Here's What Happens to Most IPO Stocks in the First Week.
CBRS.description: Anthropic completed the largest IPO ever, raising close to $120 billion, with its stock jumping 17% on the first day before falling 10% on the second day. Historical data shows IPO stocks gain an average of 19% on their first day but typically underperform the market index by 21% over three years, suggesting investors should wait for the initial hype to subside before buying.

CBRS.headline: Why Did Cerebras Stock Soar Today?
CBRS.description: Cerebras stock surged 19.2% following Nvidia's announcement that Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO, with Nvidia shares jumping 35.5%. However, the article argues this rally may be misguided, as Cerebras is actually a direct competitor to Nvidia rather than a dependent. The author suggests that Nvidia's revival is bad news for Cerebras and recommends Nvidia stock over Cerebras based on valuation metrics.

MU.headline: Why Micron Stock Dove Today
MU.description: Micron Technology stock plummeted 11.7% after BNP Paribas analyst Karl Ackerman downgraded the chipmaker from outperform to neutral and slashed his price target from $1,700 to $775. The analyst expressed concerns that memory chip supply will outpace demand by mid-2027, leading to average selling price declines earlier than previously expected. Despite the stock's 48% decline from recent peaks and attractive valuation at 8x earnings, cyclicality concerns persist in the AI chip sector.

MU.headline: Semiconductor Market to Reach USD 1,277.45 Billion by 2035 as AI Accelerators, High-Bandwidth Memory and Leading-Edge Foundry Capacity Drive the Next Chip Cycl
MU.description: The global semiconductor market is valued at USD 676.06 billion in 2026 and is projected to reach USD 1,277.45 billion by 2035, growing at a 7.36% CAGR. AI data centers are the strongest demand engine, with memory shortages and advanced foundry capacity as key constraints. Asia Pacific holds 52.93% market share while North America is the fastest-growing region. Automotive is expected to be the fastest-growing application segment.

MU.headline: SNDK's Data Center Revenues Gain Momentum on AI Demand: What's Ahead?
MU.description: SanDisk's data center revenues surged 1,682% year-over-year to $4.8 billion in Q1 fiscal 2027, driven by AI inference and growing KV cache requirements for high-capacity storage. The company is expanding supply and advancing next-generation BiCS technologies. SanDisk's total revenues reached $11.031 billion with an 85.1% non-GAAP gross margin, though it faces competition from Seagate and Micron in the data center storage market.

MU.headline: Micron Stock Soared on Monday. I'd Still Buy It, a Little at a Time.
MU.description: Micron Technology's stock surged 19% on November 23 following Nvidia's announcement of Jensen Huang's return as CEO. Despite the rally, analyst Daniel Sparks recommends buying Micron gradually, noting the company trades at under 5x earnings with strong guidance for fiscal 2027, including expected sequential revenue growth and 75% of shipments already committed by customers.

MU.headline: Sandisk Plunges 44% in a Month: Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
MU.description: SanDisk shares have dropped 44.1% in a month due to concerns about profit margin sustainability, moderating NAND pricing growth, and slowing sequential revenue growth, particularly weakness in consumer markets. However, the company benefits from surging AI-driven data center demand with fiscal Q1 data center revenues up 1,682% year-over-year to $4.8 billion, long-term customer agreements, and an attractive valuation at 3.15X forward P/E. MU.headline: Should You Invest in the First Trust NASDAQ Semiconductor ETF (FTXL)?
MU.description: The First Trust NASDAQ Semiconductor ETF (FTXL) is recommended as a Strong Buy option for investors seeking exposure to the semiconductor sector. The ETF has delivered strong performance with a 47.29% gain year-to-date and 67.42% over the past year, though it carries higher volatility with a beta of 1.83. With a 0.6% expense ratio and concentrated holdings in major semiconductor companies, FTXL is positioned favorably compared to its sector peers.

MU.headline: Stock Market News for Nov 24, 2026
MU.description: U.S. stock markets surged on Monday following NVIDIA's reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang. The Dow Jones, Nasdaq, and S&P 500 all closed significantly higher, with the Nasdaq climbing 6.5% and the S&P 500 rising 4.7%. NVIDIA stock soared 31.5%, and other AI-related semiconductor companies also experienced substantial gains. Economic data showed manufacturing and services PMI readings remained in expansion territory but declined from October levels.

MU.headline: Black Friday Comes to Tech Stocks: 3 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Names I’d Buy on Sale
MU.description: The article highlights three AI-related semiconductor stocks trading at attractive valuations ahead of Black Friday: Micron Technology benefits from strong AI-driven demand for high bandwidth memory with supply constraints; Nvidia maintains leadership in AI infrastructure with 75% projected revenue growth and CEO Jensen Huang's return; and Broadcom leads in custom AI chip development with significant growth potential from major tech customers.

MU.headline: How to Invest in Humanoid Robots: 3 Stocks to Watch
MU.description: As humanoid robots approach mainstream adoption, three tech giants are positioned to benefit from the boom. Tesla is developing its Optimus robot with plans to deliver in late 2027, Nvidia's AI chips are foundational to robotics technology, and Micron's memory chips are essential for robot functionality. All three companies offer established ways to gain exposure to the humanoid robotics market.

MU.headline: The Nasdaq Just Had Its Best Day Since April 2025. Anthropic Stock Fell Anyway.
MU.description: While the Nasdaq Composite posted its best day since April 2025 following Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO, Anthropic stock fell 1.4% despite opening up 5.4%. The decline reflects concerns that open-weight AI models, which China currently leads in, pose a significant threat to Anthropic's closed-model business strategy and growth prospects.

IREN.headline: Stock Market Today, Nov. 23: CoreWeave Surges 22% as Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
IREN.description: CoreWeave surged 22% to $48.33 on November 23, 2026, following renewed AI sector optimism after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. The broader market rallied with the S&P 500 up 4.73% and Nasdaq up 6.51%. CoreWeave's strong performance was driven by heavy trading volume and investor confidence in AI infrastructure demand, supported by Nvidia's $6 billion commitment to the company through 2032.

APLD.headline: PENG vs. APLD: Which AI Infrastructure Stock Is the Better Investment?
APLD.description: Penguin Solutions (PENG) emerges as the stronger AI infrastructure investment compared to Applied Digital (APLD). PENG demonstrates robust revenue growth of 68% with expanding profitability and positive earnings projections, trading at an attractive 1.33X P/S ratio. In contrast, APLD faces significant headwinds including a $221 million net loss, debt exceeding $6.26 billion, and widening projected losses, despite 322% revenue growth. APLD.headline: Applied Digital Secures New 150 MW, 18-Year Lease with Tier-One Investment-Grade Hyperscaler, Bringing Contracted Base-Term Revenue Above $41 Billion
APLD.description: Applied Digital announced an new 18-year lease agreement with a tier-one investment-grade hyperscaler for 150 MW of AI data center capacity, generating approximately $5.4 billion in base-term contracted revenue ($12.7 billion with renewal options). This brings the company's total contracted base-term lease revenue above $41 billion ($100 billion with all options exercised). MTSI.headline: Here's Why M/A-Com (MTSI) Is a Great 'Buy the Bottom' Stock Now
MTSI.description: M/A-Com (MTSI) has formed a hammer chart pattern after a 5% decline over four weeks, signaling potential trend reversal. The stock is supported by strong fundamental indicators including a 15.2% upward revision in consensus EPS estimates over the last 30 days and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) rating, suggesting improved company prospects.
